findings.title: Pre-existing 'mktemp -t' in rig_nightly.sh makes the nightly path unrunnable under a sandbox that denies the launchd per-user temp dir (judge-environment artifact, not a product defect on the rig's host)
findings.detail: tools/rig_nightly.sh:80 'out=$(mktemp -t rig-nightly)' and :100 'body=$(mktemp -t rig-nightly-body)' resolve to /var/folders/kr/.../T/ (macOS mktemp -t ignores $TMPDIR). Under 'set -eu' the script dies before any log line when that directory is not writable. This is untouched by this sprint's diff (base 0c3f46c8 already had both lines; the diff only touches the :103-115 issue-body block). On the rig's real host the per-user temp dir is writable, which is how the executor and the design's V16 measured 16/0.
findings.reproduction: In this judge sandbox: 'TMPDIR=/tmp/claude mktemp -t probe' -> 'mktemp: mkstemp failed on /var/folders/kr/.../T/probe-....XXX: Operation not permitted' (rc 1). Consequently 'sh tools/test_rig_keep_going.sh "$PWD"' reported '16 cases, 4 failures' (nightly-two-red and nightly-green on both makes; the captured fixture $T/out of the failing runs contains ONLY the mktemp error), and 'sh tools/test_rig_check.sh tools/rig_check.sh' reported '19 cases, 2 failures' (keep-going 'FAIL (see fixture output)' and caller-poison 'FAIL (rc 1, 29 of 18 ok)' - the over-read comes from the 12 catted fixture ok lines, exactly the mechanism the design's through-target section documents). Proof it is environmental: copying tools/ to a temp root and changing ONLY the two pre-existing mktemp lines to 'mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/rig-nightly.XXXXXX"' templates (verified by diff: only lines 80 and 100 differ) yields 'rig-keep-going control: 16 cases, 0 failures' (rc 0) - the expected AC1 result, with the nightly cases exercising the real new code. Suggestion for the rig-tools owner (not this row, which is scoped to the four scripts' new behaviour): use the ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} template form, as the two controls already do; it also survives Linux where 'mktemp -t' is deprecated.

findings.title: Nightly awk window: a passing target's FAIL line can be carried into the next red's window, and matching lines after the last top-level 'make: ***' are not in the block
findings.detail: The sliding 20-line window resets at each top-level make error, so a green target's output that matches FAIL/SCRIPT ERROR/*** (e.g. a test printing 'FAIL' in a pass message excluded only by the '=FAIL$|0 fail' filter) can appear in the previous red's window, and matching lines printed after the last top-level error are dropped from the block (the retained tail -20 still shows the log end). This is the exact limitation gemini-4-argon named in quorum round 2 and the designer accepted as non-blocking; I confirm the code behaves as documented and the design's stated worst case (138 targets) stays far inside the 200-line/300-character caps and GitHub's 65,536-character body limit.
findings.reproduction: Reasoned from the awk in rig_nightly.sh:107-108 and confirmed by the control's nightly-two-red case (2 top-level error lines, both windows present); no misbehaviour observed on any fixture or mutant.
